subject: Kickoff: Private VPC control-plane / data-plane resilience review
messages:
From: Paul Jenkins <pjenkins@coreedge.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Anita Sharma <anita.sharma@acmebank.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff: Private VPC control-plane / data-plane resilience review

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking this on. Per our call earlier this week, Acme wants to validate the deployed control-plane/data-plane boundary for their private VPC (on-prem + transit VPC in AWS). The key objectives for the review:

- Confirm control-plane management channels (API, heartbeat, control sync) are isolated and have predictable egress policies.
- Validate data-plane egress demarcation and failover behavior during regional outage / peering loss.
- Review TLS/mTLS trust anchoring between the control plane (Redwood control instances) and on-prem inference nodes.
- Confirm SKMS/KMS access patterns and token lifetime for certificate rotation.

I've attached an initial reference diagram (vpc-control-dataplane-diagram-v1.svg) that shows our proposed demarcation and a basic failover path. Could the Redwood infra team review and comment on:

1) Any missing hop you need (e.g., control-plane proxies, NAT, egress gateway)?
2) Where KV cache replication or model pull happens (we've marked a generic 'model-sync' arrow).
3) Recommended circuit breakers/timeouts for long-polling control traffic.

Can we target a short sync today or tomorrow? Anita from Acme is cc'd and can confirm scheduling.

Attachments: vpc-control-dataplane-diagram-v1.svg (diagram, 1.2MB)

Cheers,
Paul Jenkins
Principal Solutions Architect | CoreEdge Systems
pjenkins@coreedge.com | +1 415-555-0123

Subject: Re: Kickoff: Private VPC control-plane / data-plane resilience review

Paul / Anita — thanks for the clear primer and the diagram. Quick read-through notes before we set a meeting:

- High level we like the demarcation. Two immediate asks: (a) can we get the CIDR ranges for the transit VPC peering and the on-prem NAT to annotate firewall rules; (b) confirm whether the control plane will be reachable from a single public egress or via dedicated interconnect.

- For the control-plane heartbeat: we recommend separating the management channel onto a dedicated TLS port with mutual auth (mTLS). We typically put a short-lived client cert for the node agent (TTL ~24h) and use a gateway to perform cert validation off-host.

- On model-sync: need clarity on whether model artifacts are pulled directly from Redwood object storage or proxied through Acme's internal artifact registry. Proxying through Acme reduces outbound egress but adds a single point of failure — we'll include fallback to host pull in the resilience plan.

- Circuit breakers/timeouts: suggest 30s initial request timeout, exponential backoff with a max of 5 retries for control RPCs, and a separate ping/heartbeat interval of 20s with 3 missed heartbeats = node unhealthy. We'll put these in the checklist.

Can we do a 30 minute sync today at 2pm PT? If that works for everyone I'll send a calendar invite and a one-pager agenda.

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

Looping in a couple of control-plane design items from Product/Security that should be in scope for the review:

- Audit logging: we need a clear path for immutable control-plane audit logs to stream back to Acme's SIEM (log-forwarder or syslog). Include retention SLA (default 90 days) and KMS envelope requirements.

- Egress gateway: if Acme wants to egress through a transit VPC appliance, we need the IP allowlist and a small NAT/TLS health-check endpoint for L7 probes.

- Cert rotation: include a short runbook for emergency rollback if a cert rotation causes mass agent disconnects. We should also validate HSM/KMS access from the control-plane components (no long-lived service principals).

- Load-shedding: detail how the control-plane prioritizes health-related messages vs low-priority telemetry during a surge. We propose a simple prioritization queue (heartbeat & critical control > model metadata > telemetry).

I'll bring a one-page checklist to the sync. 2pm PT works for me.

Lauren Bishop

Also attached a resilience checklist (resilience-checklist.xlsx) with preliminary TTLs/timeouts.

Subject: Re: Kickoff: Private VPC control-plane / data-plane resilience review — notes & actions

Great sync yesterday — summary and action items below. Please reply if I've missed anything.

Meeting minutes (short):
- Confirmed demarcation: control-plane traffic from node agents uses dedicated mTLS port 8443 -> control-plane gateway in transit VPC.
- Data-plane egress: primary via transit VPC appliance; secondary via direct interconnect. Model artifacts proxied by Acme registry with Redwood fallback.
- Cert rotation: short-lived node certs (24h TTL), automated rotation with canary rollout. Emergency rollback runbook required.
- Heartbeat/circuit-breaker policy agreed: 20s heartbeat, 3 missed = unhealthy; 30s RPC timeout, 5 retries max (exp backoff).
- Audit logs: they will be forwarded to Acme SIEM; retention and KMS envelope requirements noted.

Action items:
1) Redwood (Rishi/Aditya): produce final annotated reference diagram (control-plane + data-plane) that includes specific CIDR ranges and NAT egress rules. Deliverable: vpc-control-dataplane-diagram-v3.svg. ETA: 2027-04-29 EOD.
2) Redwood (Lauren): publish resilience checklist as a runbook entry in Confluence with rollback steps and load-shedding policy. ETA: 2027-04-28.
3) Acme (Anita/CoreEdge): share read-only HSM service account details and transit VPC ip allowlist. ETA: 2027-04-26.
4) Joint: schedule a dry-run test for failover (target window: week of 2027-05-10).

Related artifacts (links): https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/cp/ACME-VPC-REVIEW-8421

Attachments included in this thread for reference: vpc-control-dataplane-diagram-v1.svg, vpc-control-dataplane-diagram-v2.svg, resilience-checklist.xlsx

Thanks everyone — I'll open a shared Confluence page and drop the first-pass diagram there.

Best,
